paragraphs: Here's what I take from this one, friend. Baruch was worn out, and he said so out loud: "Woe is me…" (Jeremiah 45:3). The LORD didn't scold him for it. He quoted Baruch's own words right back, which tells me He was listening to every groan.

Then comes the hard part. The LORD says He will "demolish what I have built and uproot what I have planted," and to Baruch He says, "do you seek great things for yourself? Stop seeking!" (Jeremiah 45:4-5). I think that stings a little, because I know how easy it is to chase the FANCIEST cookie in the Dorinverse and forget who the bakery is for. Big dreams for ourselves can crowd out the thing God is actually doing.

And look at what Baruch gets in place of great things. The LORD says, "wherever you go, I will grant your life as a spoil of war" (Jeremiah 45:5). It's not a palace, friend, it's his life, promised to him by name. So the next time you're worn out and tempted to reach for more, remember that the God who heard Baruch's groaning is the same God who listens to yours.
